# ShutCap

> ShutCap is a free, open-source Windows 10/11 app that turns the PC off once each night, at a time the user chooses. It warns first, has an emergency cancel, and never locks the user out. Current version: 2.1.0 (27 November 2026). MIT licence.

## Facts

- What it does: the user picks a nightly shutdown time on a dial. By default ShutCap warns 45 and 25 minutes before, shows a curfew window with a countdown 15 minutes before, and at the chosen time runs `shutdown /s /t 60` (no `/f`), so Windows gives apps 60 seconds to close.
- Emergency cancel: in the curfew window, "I have an emergency" → write a reason → "Cancel tonight's shutdown". Tonight only; the reason is saved to History.
- No lockout: it shuts down at most once per night. If the PC is turned on again after the curfew starts, ShutCap does nothing more that night.
- Practice mode is on at first: warnings show, but the PC stays on until the user turns Practice mode off in Settings.
- Privacy: no account, no telemetry, no cloud service. Optional phone alerts via ntfy.sh, off by default.
- Requirements: Windows 10 or 11 with Microsoft Edge WebView2 (included in Windows 11). No administrator rights.
- Install: download `ShutCap-Setup.exe` (46 MB). The installer is not code-signed, so SmartScreen may warn: More info → Run anyway.
- Uninstall: Settings > Apps > Installed apps > ShutCap > Uninstall.
- Earlier name: versions 1.x were called OFFLINE 11.
